extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification containing 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images in each class. The dataset features high within-class diversity, between-class similarity, and big variations in translation, spatial resolution, viewpoint, object pose, illumination, background, and occlusion.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset consists of 31,500 remote sensing images extracted from Google Earth by experts in remote sensing image interpretation. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales. The 31,500 images cover more than 100 countries and regions all over the world, including developing, transition, and highly developed economies. Scene classes were selected by first investigating existing datasets to form 30 widely-used categories, then searching academic databases for keywords related to land cover/use classification and geospatial analysis to select 15 additional meaningful scene classes, resulting in 45 total classes with 700 images each.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from Google Earth, which maps the Earth by the superimposition of images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography and geographic information system (GIS) onto a 3D globe. The spatial resolution varies from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel for most scene classes except for island, lake, mountain, and snowberg which have lower spatial resolutions. Images are 256×256 pixels in RGB color space.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual annotation by agricultural researchers for Brazilian Coffee Scene Dataset. For coffee dataset: tiles with at least 85% of coffee pixels were assigned to the coffee class; tiles with less than 10% of coffee pixels were assigned to the non-coffee class.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limitations in spatial resolution for certain scene classes, with spatial resolution varying from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel for most scene classes except for island, lake, mountain, and snowberg classes that have lower spatial resolutions. The paper also notes that scene classification methods relying only on overhead imagery have shortcomings that could be complemented by social media and spatial technology data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables intelligent earth observation and has applications in natural hazards detection, land use and land cover determination, geospatial object detection, geographic image retrieval, vegetation mapping, environment monitoring, and urban planning.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset covers images from more than 100 countries and regions all over the world, including developing, transition, and highly developed economies, which may implicitly contain geographic and socio-economic information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed as a benchmark for remote sensing image scene classification, enabling the development and evaluation of data-driven algorithms including deep learning methods. It can be used for training, testing, and validation of scene classification systems.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Dropout method was employed to prevent over-fitting in fully-connected layers. Rotation-invariant CNN (RICNN) model was developed by imposing a regularization constraint term which explicitly enforces the feature representations of training samples before and after rotation to be mapped close to each other.
